problem_statement: When the function-name prefix feature is enabled for a log level, log output should print the source name followed by a dot and the function name (e.g. "<dbg> src.test_levels: ...") so that the message is prefixed with the function it came from. Instead, for a level whose function-name prefix is enabled the output is printed as if the function prefix were not used ("<dbg> src: ..."), using a colon and omitting the function name entirely, so callers cannot see which function produced the log line.

verification.reason: The statement conveys the desired output format but omits the exact per-level Kconfig names and is ambiguous about whether the function name should be added by log output or already present in the message. These can be repaired by adding public interface and behavior details without prescribing the implementation.

problems.detail: The hidden test uses CONFIG_LOG_FUNC_NAME_PREFIX_ERR, CONFIG_LOG_FUNC_NAME_PREFIX_WRN, CONFIG_LOG_FUNC_NAME_PREFIX_INF, and CONFIG_LOG_FUNC_NAME_PREFIX_DBG to decide per-level behavior, but the statement only refers generically to the function-name prefix feature.

The statement is ambiguous about where the function name comes from: the hidden test requires the function name to already be part of the log message and the log output to change the source suffix from a colon to a dot, rather than duplicating the function name in the prefix.
The hidden colors test checks the same dot/colon behavior when color codes are present, but the statement does not mention that the required behavior must also hold with color output.

leak_check.leak_detail: The phrase about the function name already being present in the log message and the output not adding it again hints at the internal data flow, but it is close to an observable interface property and can be reworded to the final-output requirement.
leak_check.suggested_statement:
When the function-name prefix feature is enabled for a log level, log output should print the source name followed by a dot and the function name (e.g. '<dbg> src.test_levels: ...') so that the message is prefixed with the function it came from. Instead, for a level whose function-name prefix is enabled the output is printed as if the function prefix were not used ('<dbg> src: ...'), using a colon and omitting the function name entirely, so callers cannot see which function produced the log line.

The per-level feature is controlled by CONFIG_LOG_FUNC_NAME_PREFIX_ERR, CONFIG_LOG_FUNC_NAME_PREFIX_WRN, CONFIG_LOG_FUNC_NAME_PREFIX_INF, and CONFIG_LOG_FUNC_NAME_PREFIX_DBG. For an enabled level, the complete output must contain the function name exactly once, in the form '<level> source.function: message', with a dot after the source name, while a disabled level keeps '<level> source: message'. This behavior must also apply when color codes are included, preserving the existing color placement around the line.
